Surah Quraysh is Meccan. [Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The verse 'For the covenants of Quraysh' was revealed in Makkah." See al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/634.]

﷽

* *

﴿For the covenant of Quraysh﴾. Abu Ja'far recited "Lifaf" without a hamza, "ilafihim," seeking lightness. Ibn 'Amir recited "la-lāf" with a short (mukhtalasah) hamza, without a yā' after it [on the pattern of "li-ghilaf"]. The others recited with a lengthened (mushba'ah) hamza and a yā' after it. All of them, except Abu Ja'far, agreed on "ilafihim" having a yā' after the hamza, except that 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Fulayh, from Ibn Kathir, recited "ilfihim" with the lam sukun and without a yā'.

Some scholars counted Surat al-Fil and this surah as one surah; among them Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who placed no separation between them in his codex. They said: the lam in "li-ilaf" is connected to the surah before it, because Allah, exalted is He, reminded the people of Makkah of His great blessing upon them in what He did to the Abyssinians, and said: ﴿For the covenant of Quraysh﴾. [See: Fath al-Bari: 8/730.]

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: He made them like eaten chaff for the covenant of Quraysh, i.e., He intends to destroy the people of the elephant so that Quraysh and what they had grown accustomed to of the journey of winter and summer may remain. [In "B" it reads: "destroy the companions of the elephant."] [In "A": Al-Farra' said: ... Returning to al-Farra' 3/293, you find his words: "As if he said: that is for His blessing upon them in the journey of winter and summer."]

Mujahid said: they became accustomed to that, so it was not hard for them in winter and summer. [See: Fath al-Bari: 8/730.]

The majority hold that they are two surahs. They differed regarding the cause that brings the lam in His saying "li-ilaf." Al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash said: it is the lam of wonder (lam al-ta'ajjub). It means: wonder at the covenant of Quraysh regarding the journey of winter and summer, and their abandonment of the worship of the Lord of this House. Then He commanded them to worship Him, just as you say in speech to Zayd, with our honoring him, in the manner of wonder: "Wonder at that!" When the Arabs use this lam, they suffice with it as evidence of wonder at the act being displayed.

Al-Zajjaj said: it refers back to what follows it; its estimate is: "So let them worship the Lord of this House, for their covenant regarding the journey of winter and summer."

Ibn 'Uyaynah [in B: Abu 'Ubaydah] said: it is for My blessing upon Quraysh.

Quraysh are the descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah, and everyone born of al-Nadr is Qurashi, and whoever is not born of al-Nadr is not Qurashi.

Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni informed us; Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Shurayk al-Shafi'i informed us; 'Abdullah ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jawrabadhi informed us; Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Sadafi narrated to us; Bishr ibn Bakr informed us, from al-Awza'i; Shaddad Abu 'Ammar narrated to me; Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah chose Kinanah from the descendants of Isma'il, and chose from Kinanah Quraysh, and chose from Quraysh the Banu Hashim, and chose me from the Banu Hashim." [Related by Muslim in the Book of Virtues, chapter on the excellence of the lineage of the Prophet (ﷺ), no. (2276): 4/1782; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/194.]

They were named Quraysh from al-Qarsh, and al-Taqarrush, which is earning and gathering. It is said: "So-and-so yaqrishu for his dependents and yaqtarishu," meaning he earns. They were merchants, eager for gathering wealth and generosity.

Abu Rayhanah said: [Ibn Kathir mentioned it in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 2/202, attributing it to al-Bayhaqi. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/638.] Mu'awiyah asked 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas: Why was Quraysh named Quraysh? He said: After a creature in the sea, among its greatest creatures, called al-Qirsh, which passes by nothing of the lean or the fat except that it eats it; it eats and is not eaten, and it rises and is not overcome. He said: Do the Arabs know that in their poetry? He said: Yes, and he recited the verses of al-Jumahi:

And Quraysh are those who dwell in the sea,
by them Quraysh was named "Quraysh."

Empowered by height in the deep of the sea,
over all the seas, armies.

It eats the lean and the fat and leaves not
in it for the two-winged, a feather.

Thus in the Book, the tribe of Quraysh,
they devour the lands with swift consumption [kamish, meaning quickly].

And for them at the end of time is a prophet,
who multiplies killing among them and wounds.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 106, verse 2–4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their journeys (ilaf) in the winter and the summer﴾. "Ilafihim" is a substitute (badal) for the first "ilaf". "Rihlata" is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: their departing on the journey of winter and summer.

ʿIkrimah and Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "They used to spend the winter in Makkah and the summer in al-Ta'if, so Allah exalted commanded them to remain in the sanctuary (Haram) and worship the Lord of this House." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/308, and al-Nasa'i in al-Tafsir 2/552 with a good chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/635 to Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah.]]

Others said: they had two journeys each year for trade: one in the winter to Yemen, because it is warmer, and the other in the summer to Syria.

The Haram was a barren valley with neither crops nor livestock, and the Quraysh lived by their trade and their journeys. No one would harm them, and they would say: "The Quraysh are the inhabitants of Allah's Sanctuary and the custodians of His House. If not for the two journeys, they would have had no settlement in Makkah, and if not for the security granted by the neighbourhood of the House, they would not have been able to conduct their affairs." It was hard for them to travel back and forth to Yemen and Syria, so Tabalah and Jarash in the lands of Yemen became fertile, and they carried food to Makkah: the people of the coast by ships across the sea, and the people of the land by camels and donkeys. The people of the coast unloaded at Jeddah, and the people of the land at al-Muhassab. Syria also became fertile, so they carried food to Makkah and unloaded it at al-Abtah. They obtained provisions nearby, and Allah spared them the burden of the two journeys, and commanded them to worship the Lord of the House, saying: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House﴾, that is, the Ka'bah.

﴿Who fed them against hunger﴾, that is, after hunger, by bringing provisions to Makkah. ﴿And made them secure from fear﴾ through the Haram, and because they were people of Makkah, so that no one would molest them on their journeys.

ʿAta' narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "They were in hardship and famine until Hashim gathered them for the two journeys, and they would divide their profit between the poor and the rich, so that their poor was like their rich."

al-Kalbi said: [[See al-Tabari: 2/252; al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 2/253.]] The first to carry al-Samra' [[In "A" it reads "al-Samn" (ghee).]] from Syria and to send camels on that route was Hashim ibn ʿAbd Manaf, and about him the poet says [[He is Ibn al-Zaba'ri, as in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah and al-Tabari.]]:

"Say to him who seeks generosity and bounty: Why did you not pass by the family of ʿAbd Manaf?"

"Why did you not pass by them seeking their hospitality? They would have protected you from harm and from want,"

"The ones who gather (the crushed bread), though none gathers it, and who say: Come, for the guests,"

"And who mix their poor with their rich, until their poor is like one who is sufficient,"

"And who fulfil every true promise, and who set out on the journey of ilaf,"

"ʿAmr [al-ʿUla] [[In "A" "al-ʿali". In al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah and al-Tabari: "alladhi".]] who crushed the bread for his people, while the men of Makkah were in drought and lean,"

"Two journeys he established for himself and his people: the journey of winter and the journey of summer."

Mujahid? No: al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' and Sufyan said: "And made them secure from fear" means from fear of leprosy, so that leprosy would not afflict them in their land.
